verses.text: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him in God’s likeness.
He created them male and female, and blessed them. On the day they were created, he named them “Adam”.
Adam lived one hundred thirty years, and became the father of a son in his own likeness, after his image, and named him Seth.
The days of Adam after he became the father of Seth were eight hundred years, and he became the father of other sons and daughters.
All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred thirty years, then he died.
Seth lived one hundred five years, then became the father of Enosh.
Seth lived after he became the father of Enosh eight hundred seven years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Seth were nine hundred twelve years, then he died.
Enosh lived ninety years, and became the father of Kenan.
Enosh lived after he became the father of Kenan, eight hundred fifteen years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Enosh were nine hundred five years, then he died.
Kenan lived seventy years, then became the father of Mahalalel.
Kenan lived after he became the father of Mahalalel eight hundred forty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters
and all of the days of Kenan were nine hundred ten years, then he died.
Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Jared.
Mahalalel lived after he became the father of Jared eight hundred thirty years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred ninety-five years, then he died.
Jared lived one hundred sixty-two years, then became the father of Enoch.
Jared lived after he became the father of Enoch eight hundred years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All of the days of Jared were nine hundred sixty-two years, then he died.
Enoch lived sixty-five years, then became the father of Methuselah.
After Methuselah’s birth, Enoch walked with God for three hundred years, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
All the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty-five years.
Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.
Methuselah lived one hundred eighty-seven years, then became the father of Lamech.
Methuselah lived after he became the father of Lamech seven hundred eighty-two years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty-nine years, then he died.
Lamech lived one hundred eighty-two years, then became the father of a son.
He named him Noah, saying, “This one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands, caused by the ground which Yahweh has cursed.”
Lamech lived after he became the father of Noah five hundred ninety-five years, and became the father of other sons and daughters.
All the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy-seven years, then he died.
Noah was five hundred years old, then Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

footnotes.content: I love that Moses calls this 'the book of the generations of Adam.' Before he lists deaths, he reminds us we were made in God's likeness. That image is still true of us, though marred by sin, and it points us all the more to our true Adam, Jesus Christ, who perfectly bears that likeness for us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God made them male and female and blessed them. How precious that our origin is not accident, but blessing. Long before the curse's weight, God spoke goodness over humanity, and that original blessing still whispers of the greater blessing we have in union with Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adam bore a son in his own likeness, after his image - and Scripture marks it solemnly. The image remains, but now it carries the mark of mortality. For all his long years, the refrain comes: 'then he died.' How thankful I am that another Son, the true Image of God, took our mortality to Himself to give us life that death cannot touch.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seth's line is the line of hope - the godly seed promised after Abel. Yet here too, generation after generation, the same sentence falls: 'then he died.' I have walked long enough to know death claims young and old alike. That is why the God who kept this line going was quietly preserving the way to Jesus, the only One who has conquered the grave.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Enosh came after Seth, and men began to call on the name of the Lord in his days (Genesis 4:26). Even in a dying world, grace stirred hearts to pray. Still, for all those prayers and long lives, 'he died.' I find comfort knowing our prayers today rest on the prayers of our great High Priest, Jesus, who ever lives to intercede for His own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kenan's days stretch nearly a millennium, yet they are measured and ended by death. How easy it is for us to count years instead of counting God's faithfulness. I have learned to do the latter. The faithfulness of God is what carried this line from Adam to Noah to Christ, and it carries His people still, one day at a time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mahalalel lived long, but his life is summed up in begetting, living, and dying. There is no boast here - only faithfulness in the ordinary. As a grandparent, I rejoice more in hidden faithfulness than in fame. Our Lord, who walked hidden years in Nazareth, sees and treasures every act of love done for His sake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jared's years were many, yet the record gives us little more than generations and death. That is the mercy of Scripture - it shows us that a life can be quietly used by God to bring the next link in His redemptive plan. I take courage: the Lord uses obscure faithfulness to preserve a people for Himself and to bring forth our Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Enoch walked with God - two words that say more than all his years could. In a world where everyone else died, Enoch's end was different: God took him. Hebrews tells us he was taken so that he would not see death, commended as one who pleased God. I long for that same walk with my Savior, knowing that because He was taken up for me, I too will be caught up to be with Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Methuselah holds the record for longest life - nine hundred sixty-nine years. Yet even Methuselah died. How sobering that the oldest man in the Bible is still under the sentence of Genesis 3. I take comfort that the youngest of God's children, by faith in Jesus, has a life that never ends - eternal life, already ours in our risen Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lamech named his son Noah, saying he would comfort us in our toil. It was a small glimmer of hope in a groaning world. God did bring relief through Noah in his day, but our greater Noah - Jesus, our rest and our refuge - has borne the toil and curse for us. In Him, the weary find true comfort for their souls, both now and forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
